On Christmas Eve, 1914, soldiers who had spent months trying to kill each other put down their rifles and started to sing.
It began in the German trenches, with tiny Christmas trees lit by candles.
Then the Germans began to sing Silent Night.
The British soldiers listened in silence. And then they sang back.
At dawn, men from both sides climbed out of their trenches, with their hands in the air, and walked into no man's land.
They shook hands. They swapped cigarettes, chocolate, and buttons from their uniforms.
They even buried their dead together.
Then someone found a ball. And hundreds of men started to play football in the mud.
Their generals were furious. They gave orders to make sure it never happened again.
It never did, not on that scale.
But for one night, and one morning, a war stopped, because enemies chose to be human.
